scores.claim_text: Ford-class aircraft carrier — CW names this as a forward shipbuilding-funded revenue program.
scores.interpretation: Navy shipbuilding (SCN) procurement line items for CVN-78/Ford-class are not covered in the v1 J-Book corpus (corpus focuses on RDT&E + select Air Force/Space/SOCOM procurement). Per heuristic 7, NOT_FOUND for a clearly out-of-scope corpus area is a coverage gap, not a red flag. Independently, USAspending shows real CW Naval Sea Systems Command awards (e.g., N0002405C4217 Cheswick — ships propulsion components), corroborating the underlying revenue stream is real. No divergence detected; downgrade to UNVERIFIABLE (no negative evidence).

scores.claim_text: Columbia-class submarine — CW names this as a forward shipbuilding revenue program.
scores.interpretation: Navy SSBN procurement (Columbia-class) sits in the Navy SCN account / Trident-style PE structure, which is out of the v1 J-Book corpus scope. USAspending confirms CW Electro-Mechanical receives NAVSEA contracts for motors/actuators/coolant pumps; Columbia is well-known bipartisan-supported priority. NOT_FOUND here is a corpus coverage gap, not a divergence.

scores.claim_text: Virginia-class submarine — CW names this as a forward shipbuilding revenue program.
scores.interpretation: Navy SSN-774 procurement is out of v1 J-Book corpus scope. USAspending shows continuing CW NAVSEA awards consistent with Virginia-class supplier role. No divergence; coverage gap, not a red flag (heuristic 7).

scores.claim_text: Westinghouse AP1000 RCPs and control rod drive mechanisms — CW names AP1000 as a forward commercial-nuclear revenue platform.
scores.interpretation: AP1000 deployments are funded primarily by utility-owners and NRC-licensed customers (commercial reactors); DOE involvement is via ARDP/Loan Programs Office, neither of which is fully in v1 DOE Office of Science corpus. The CW AP1000 RCP claim is forward-looking and dependent on new Vogtle-style new-builds — neither corroborated nor refuted by available M-sources. Mark UNVERIFIABLE (heuristic 7).

scores.claim_text: Advanced Small Modular Reactors (SMR) — CW asserts forward pipeline support for design and deployment.
scores.interpretation: DOE Office of Nuclear Energy (NE) SMR / ARDP line items are not in the v1 DOE corpus (Office of Science only). CW SMR claim is broad and forward-looking (design + deployment 'support'), not tied to a specific customer or contract. Coverage gap; UNVERIFIABLE.

scores.claim_text: C5ISR / electronic warfare / encryption / unmanned / communications — CW expects increased DoD funding across these categories.
scores.interpretation: At least one named sub-category (Electronic Warfare) the company points to is FUNDED_STEADY in the J-Book as of 2024 cutoff. The other named categories (C5ISR, unmanned, communications) are broad portfolios spanning many PEs and aren't single-program lookups; no divergence pattern observed. PASS — narrative is consistent with corpus funding signal.

pentagon_jbook(contractor_name='Curtiss-Wright') => NOT_FOUND (J-Book corpus doesn't tag CW as a primary contractor on its 410 PEs — CW is a subcomponent supplier on many platforms, not a prime)

scores.interpretation: USAspending strongly corroborates a broad cross-platform DoD presence: 2,361 historical DoD awards across multiple CW subsidiaries (CW Electro-Mechanical, CW DS, CW Defense Solutions). The J-Book primary_contractors lists do not name CW, consistent with CW's actual role (sub-tier component supplier on platforms whose primes are Lockheed/NG/GD/Boeing/HII). No divergence — claim of broad presence is corroborated by spending data. PASS.

summary.notes: All CW-specific J-Book lookups (Ford/Columbia/Virginia/AP1000/SMR/AAS/C5ISR umbrella, and contractor_name='Curtiss-Wright') return NOT_FOUND. This reflects (a) Navy SCN procurement and DOE-NE programs being out of the v1 J-Book + DOE Office-of-Science corpus scope, and (b) CW's actual role as a sub-tier component supplier (motors, RCPs, actuators, COTS embedded computing) rather than a J-Book-named prime. Where category-level J-Book lookups DID resolve (Electronic Warfare, JTNC PE 0605030F, F-35 PE 0604840F, B-21, Aerospace Propulsion), all showed FUNDED_STEADY at the 2024 cutoff, consistent with CW's forward narrative. USAspending confirms 2,361 DoD awards / $325M across multiple CW subsidiaries (CW Electro-Mechanical NAVSEA contracts for motors/actuators; CW DS PacStar contract W56JSR20C0012 base+4 option years; etc.). No J-Book divergence pattern detected at this cutoff.
